title: Prefrontal · Controlled context for enterprise AI
subtitle: A product concept and measured pilot proposal

slides.title: Put the right context behind every AI task.
slides.lead: A governed context product for your AI workflows. Reuse organizational knowledge. Control the task. Prove the value.

items.title: A reusable product
items.text: One context foundation across domain-specific workflows.

items.title: A measured pilot
items.text: Agree the baseline, quality gates and benefit owner.

slides.note: Product concept · seeking a pilot partner. Writing inspired by ASD-STE100; full compliance has not been checked.

slides.title: Every task pays for missing context.
slides.lead: Teams spend effort finding evidence, reconciling changes and reviewing AI work. A shared context product targets that repeated work.

items.title: Repeated setup
items.text: People explain definitions, ownership and exceptions again for each workflow.

items.title: Avoidable work
items.text: Irrelevant context, retries and manual reconciliation can add cost and delay.

items.title: Uncertain answers
items.text: Missing dates or conditions can make an answer unsuitable for the task.

items.title: Unclear accountability
items.text: Teams need to see which evidence, permissions and review decisions support a result.

slides.note: Buyer problem hypotheses. Measure their frequency and cost in the first workflow; industry pressure figures do not quantify them.

slides.eyebrow: Why this product · enterprise field insights
slides.title: Enterprise value needs an operating model.
slides.lead: Enterprise conference field notes connect business meaning, appropriate methods and lifecycle control. Prefrontal brings those ideas into one proposed context product.
slides.note: Source: Yashu Sharma’s independent field report, 1 September 2026. Vendor savings claims are not used as Prefrontal results.

slides.title: Four outcomes. One accountable pilot.
slides.lead: Design for cost, performance, accuracy and trust together. Agree how each outcome will be measured before implementation.
slides.note: Product objectives and proposed mechanisms. No improvement, benchmark or trust score has been established for Prefrontal.

slides.title: A context foundation around your AI workflows.
slides.lead: Prefrontal is designed to organize approved knowledge, assemble task context and preserve control as components change.

items.title: Connect your knowledge
items.text: Adapt approved documents, records and tools to shared context rules.

items.title: Keep meaning and ownership
items.text: Carry source identity, dates, exceptions, uncertainty and the responsible owner.

items.title: Fit your model strategy
items.text: Use adapters around models, retrieval and tools. Keep the context contract explicit.

items.title: Qualify each workflow
items.text: Configure domain definitions, permissions, review and acceptance cases for each customer.

slides.note: Proposed product architecture. Integrations and runtime behavior require implementation and customer-specific qualification.

slides.title: Turn approved evidence into useful task context.
slides.lead: One lifecycle carries the source, its meaning and its authority into the task. Corrections flow into the affected views.

items.title: Admit
items.text: Check source scope and access. Keep permitted originals and revisions.

items.title: Reconcile
items.text: Link claims to evidence. Preserve time, exceptions and unresolved conflicts.

items.title: Prepare
items.text: Create searchable and clear task views. Keep their dependencies visible.

items.title: Maintain
items.text: Apply corrections, access revocation and retention rules to derived views.

slides.note: Proposed lifecycle. A memory proposal becomes usable only through the agreed evidence and policy checks.

slides.title: Choose a capable path for each task.
slides.lead: Routine work may use valid cached context, retrieval or a bounded decision. Escalate when evidence or complexity requires more.

items.title: Bound the work
items.text: Limit inputs and options to the active task. Keep uncertainty visible.

items.title: Reuse with conditions
items.text: Check source versions, freshness, scope and permissions before using a cached view.

items.title: Measure the complete path
items.text: Include retrieval, reasoning, tools, retries and review in cost and latency.

items.title: Protect quality
items.text: A lower-cost path must meet the same acceptance and authority gates.

slides.note: Routing is a design proposal. No method is always cheapest; local workload measurements decide. Candidate decision models remain unqualified.

slides.title: Clear language. Preserved meaning.
slides.lead: Give the agent and reviewer a concise task view. Carry the conditions that determine the correct decision.

items.title: Preserve the decision
items.text: Keep negation, conditions, exceptions, numbers, units, dates and uncertainty.

items.title: Keep evidence available
items.text: Link derived statements to source records. Retain exact wording where it matters.

items.title: Check the rewrite
items.text: Detect omitted conditions and unsupported additions. Flag unresolved meaning.

items.title: Measure both forms
items.text: Compare task decisions from original and simplified context on difficult cases.

slides.note: STE-inspired approach. Full ASD-STE100 compliance and meaning preservation require validation; concise writing alone cannot guarantee accuracy.

slides.title: Put authority where the responsibility sits.
slides.lead: Use routine automation within approved rules. Give owners clear review points for consequential decisions and exceptions.

items.title: Source scope
items.text: Approve initial sources and material expansion of access.

items.title: Evidence conflict
items.text: Resolve disagreements that materially affect a decision.

items.title: Goal or authority ambiguity
items.text: Clarify material uncertainty about intent or permitted action.

items.title: Retention or deletion
items.text: Approve consequential choices about originals, derived views and backups.

items.title: Policy or permission change
items.text: Review changes to trusted rules, access or action authority.

items.title: Acceptance or autonomy
items.text: Accept milestone evidence and approve any broader autonomous scope.

slides.note: Proposed controls. Trusted policy enforces permission; retrieved instructions and model confidence cannot change it.

slides.title: The workflow changes. The context need travels.
slides.lead: These industry signals explain why the examples matter. Prefrontal’s proposed foundation adapts through domain definitions, connectors and review rules.
slides.note: Different units and populations. Do not combine the figures or treat them as context-product performance results.

slides.title: Turn alerts into reviewable incident briefs.
slides.lead: For network operations, connect an alert to the service, recent changes and approved next checks.
slides.note: Industry signal: observed evidence. Product workflow and buyer objective: proposed; benefits require a qualified pilot.

slides.title: Bring current evidence into connection reviews.
slides.lead: For grid teams, assemble current study references and unresolved prerequisites before an engineering decision.
slides.note: Industry signal: observed evidence. Product workflow and buyer objective: proposed; benefits require a qualified pilot.

slides.title: Keep care handoffs traceable.
slides.lead: For clinical teams, prepare a cited draft with the correct patient, dates, conflicts and responsible reviewer.
slides.note: Industry signal: observed evidence. Product workflow and buyer objective: proposed; benefits require a qualified pilot.

slides.title: Carry guest requests across every shift.
slides.lead: For hotel operations, link the request, verified room status, promises and responsible next action.
slides.note: Industry signal: observed evidence. Product workflow and buyer objective: proposed; benefits require a qualified pilot.

slides.title: Reuse the foundation. Adapt the workflow.
slides.lead: Follow one task from its evidence to its responsible owner. Domain knowledge changes; the core checks remain consistent.
slides.note: Designed for cross-industry reuse. Each deployment needs its own integrations, permissions and acceptance evidence.

slides.title: Make the economics inspectable.
slides.lead: Compare the same accepted-task target. Change the assumptions and see recurring cost, handling effort and one-time setup separately.
slides.note: Planning worksheet only. It runs arithmetic in this browser; it does not call a model or predict a customer result.

slides.title: Agree the scorecard before the pilot.
slides.lead: A lower bill is useful only when the workflow also meets its performance, quality and control requirements.
slides.note: Thresholds need buyer agreement. No product performance, accuracy, certification or realized saving is claimed.

slides.eyebrow: Protect the investment · interactive design example
slides.title: Keep the context contract when models change.
slides.lead: Explore a small contract example. Compare a replacement against the same evidence, meaning and authority checks.

items.title: Compare
items.text: Check evidence recovery, correctness, abstention, meaning, context size, latency and cost.

items.title: Approve or reject
items.text: Promote only within approved scope after agreed gates pass.

items.title: Recover
items.text: Roll back a failed candidate and resume with goals, history and verified outcomes intact.

slides.note: Browser demonstration on one fixed record. Real model migration, recovery and performance qualification remain pending.

slides.title: Start with one workflow. Expand after proof.
slides.lead: Scope the first implementation around an accountable owner and a repeatable task. Agree deliverables and exit criteria before work starts.

items.title: Frame the pilot
items.text: Choose workflow, sources, data boundary, permitted actions and benefit owner.

items.title: Establish the baseline
items.text: Record accepted-task cost, latency, review effort and failure cases.

items.title: Build the context path
items.text: Implement approved adapters, memory, task views and review boundaries.

items.title: Evaluate together
items.text: Use held-out cases and agreed load. Review quality, controls and complete costs.

items.title: Prove maintenance
items.text: Exercise source updates, access revocation, model replacement and recovery.

items.title: Decide the rollout
items.text: Review measured results and residual risks. Expand, revise or stop against agreed gates.

slides.note: Proposed pilot scope. Dates, pricing, integration effort and success thresholds require agreement; runtime capabilities are not yet delivered.

slides.title: Bring one workflow. Agree the proof.
slides.lead: Partner on a measured Prefrontal pilot. Start where repeated context work matters and a responsible owner can judge the result.

items.title: Choose the workflow
items.text: Name the user, task, current process and business consequence.

items.title: Bring the baseline
items.text: Identify current costs, time, review effort and accepted-output criteria.

items.title: Set the boundary
items.text: Approve sources, privacy, permissions, human review and retention.

items.title: Agree the decision
items.text: Define pilot deliverables, commercial terms and evidence needed to expand.

slides.note: Product concept and pilot-partner invitation. Customer value is measured in the pilot; no production service or price is represented as available today.

slides.title: Define a versioned context contract
slides.lead: The contract defines the records, meanings and rules that components exchange. Changes require compatible behavior or an explicit migration.

items.title: Source record
items.text: Stable ID, permitted original, revision, origin, scope and access rules.

items.title: Claim record
items.text: Statement, source references, conditions, uncertainty and competing claims.

items.title: Time and dependencies
items.text: Observed and valid dates; the inputs and versions used by each derived view.

items.title: Task and authority
items.text: Goal, constraints, pending decisions, permissions and intended, attempted or verified actions.

slides.note: Evidence traceability explains origin and transformation. It does not prove a source is true. Source: prov.

slides.title: Keep evidence durable and task context bounded.
slides.lead: The proposed memory design separates permitted evidence from derived views and the current task. Each selected item keeps its source and selection reason.

items.title: Evidence vault
items.text: Permitted originals and structured claims preserve history, scope and unresolved disagreements.

items.title: Rebuildable views
items.text: Search indexes, embeddings, caches, graphs and summaries derive from authorized evidence.

items.title: Working task context
items.text: Current goal, constraints, useful evidence, pending decisions and tool results fit the model input limit.

items.title: Candidate foundations
items.text: Compare OpenViking, Graphiti, Letta Code and Mem0 against actual tasks. No stack is selected.

slides.note: Local runtime, provider behavior and integration remain unverified. Sources: openviking, graphiti, letta, mem0.

slides.title: 15 responsibilities: 12 lifecycle and 3 governance
slides.lead: These are logical responsibilities. They do not require 15 agents or services.

items.title: 1–3 · Capture sources
items.text: Register sources; capture and version originals; parse and segment material.

items.title: 4–6 · Validate proposals
items.text: Classify scope and content; extract memory proposals; check evidence, time, conflicts and uncertainty.

items.title: 7–9 · Maintain usable state
items.text: Persist labeled memory and history; maintain derived indexes; resolve the active goal and constraints.

items.title: 10–12 · Support the task
items.text: Retrieve and rank permitted evidence; assemble and check STE-inspired context; apply feedback, corrections and forgetting.

items.title: 13–15 · Govern the lifecycle
items.text: Enforce policy and permissions; audit provenance; evaluate quality and reliability.

slides.note: Planning count, not a universal architecture rule. Retention applies across the lifecycle. Full external-action execution needs separate acceptance checks.

slides.title: A clear view of what is ready and what comes next.
slides.lead: The presentation and interactive examples are available. The context product still needs implementation and a qualified pilot.

items.title: Available today
items.text: Research-informed product story, source-backed industry examples and browser design demonstrations.

items.title: Pilot implementation
items.text: Approved data adapters, memory behavior, context selection and review workflows remain to be built.

items.title: Proof to earn
items.text: Demonstrate accepted-task economics, latency, accuracy, boundaries and recovery on the buyer’s workload.

items.title: Expansion decision
items.text: Use measured outcomes and owner approval. Qualify new domains and integrations before broader operation.

slides.note: This pitch does not claim deployed context infrastructure, operational results, full compliance or future-proof performance.

industries.name: Telecommunications

metric.label: Mobile network data traffic growth
metric.scope: Global mobile networks, including fixed wireless access.
metric.limitation: Traffic growth does not measure incident rates or missing context. Indexed chart: Q2 2025 = 100.
metric.definition: Fixed wireless access delivers broadband to a fixed location through a mobile network.

industries.insight: More traffic raises the importance of understanding local network conditions.
industries.problem: An alert alone cannot explain the affected service, recent change or approved response.
industries.solution: Link the alert to the right service, recent changes and current runbook. Draft cited options and prerequisites.
industries.output: Incident brief with sources, unknowns and proposed next checks.
industries.humanGate: The network operator approves any configuration change. The agent cannot grant itself access.
industries.test: Check source recovery, stale telemetry detection and reviewer corrections on historical incidents.
industries.benefit: Faster investigation with less repeated evidence gathering.
industries.buyerMetric: Measure handling time, task acceptance and permission-gate results.

industries.name: Electricity utilities

metric.label: Advanced-stage renewables awaiting connection
metric.scope: Global renewable project capacity. Utility-scale batteries are reported separately.
metric.sourceTitle: IEA · Modernising Grids in the Age of Electricity
metric.limitation: A lower-bound capacity snapshot, not a project count or capacity this system can connect.
metric.definition: GW means gigawatts, a unit of power capacity. Each plotted node represents 100 GW of the reported lower bound.

industries.insight: Connection reviews need current engineering evidence and a clear decision history.
industries.problem: An application and an old study can describe different assumptions or network states.
industries.solution: Assemble a traceable review brief. Flag conflicting revisions and missing prerequisites before engineering review.
industries.output: Connection review brief with study references and unresolved engineering questions.
industries.humanGate: A qualified engineer validates studies and limits. The operator retains connection and operating authority.
industries.test: Check evidence completeness, revision conflicts found and reviewer correction rates on historical applications.
industries.benefit: Less reconciliation across application and study versions.
industries.buyerMetric: Measure evidence completeness, review time and revision-conflict detection.

industries.name: Healthcare

metric.label: Receive / integrate outside summary records
metric.scope: U.S. non-federal acute-care hospitals. Weighted hospital-level survey estimates.
metric.limitation: Capability rates, not patient outcomes. These aggregate measures do not identify which hospitals lack integration.
metric.definition: Integrate means the electronic health record incorporates an outside summary without manual entry.

industries.insight: Receiving a record and integrating it are different capabilities.
industries.problem: A handoff still needs the correct patient, dates, source status and unresolved conflicts.
industries.solution: Prepare a cited handoff that distinguishes current evidence, conflicts and unknowns. Keep clinical decisions with the clinician.
industries.output: Draft handoff with source links and clear review questions.
industries.humanGate: The responsible clinician verifies content and makes clinical decisions. Privacy and access controls must hold.
industries.test: Use approved synthetic cases to check identity separation, temporal accuracy and clinician corrections.
industries.benefit: A clearer draft with fewer missing handoff facts.
industries.buyerMetric: Use approved cases to measure source correctness, correction effort and privacy-boundary results.

industries.name: Hospitality

metric.label: Surveyed hoteliers reported staffing shortages
metric.scope: U.S.-focused AHLA survey of 282 hotelier respondents. Self-reported; not a census.
metric.sourceTitle: AHLA / Hireology · Front Desk Feedback survey
metric.limitation: A dated respondent result, not a current estimate for all hotels. The context layer does not create staff.
metric.definition: The 100 plotted dots represent percentage points, not the 282 actual survey respondents.

industries.insight: A shift brief should carry the request, verified status, owner and next action.
industries.problem: A guest request can remain open while ownership moves between teams and shifts.
industries.task: Hand over an open room-maintenance request.
inputs: Promises already made to the guest
industries.solution: Link the guest request, room update and maintenance ticket. Draft a shift brief that marks unverified completion.
industries.output: Shift brief with verified status, owner, next action and escalation condition.
industries.humanGate: Staff verifies room readiness. A manager approves compensation or room moves under hotel policy.
industries.test: Check open-task recall, owner accuracy and false completion claims in approved shift scenarios.
industries.benefit: Fewer lost tasks when ownership moves across shifts.
industries.buyerMetric: Measure open-task recall, owner accuracy, handling time and false completion claims.

pitch.audience: Enterprise AI leaders, operations owners and pilot sponsors

conference.title: AI Enterprise Conference 2026 — Yashu Sharma’s Field Report
conference.scope: Independent field report: 19 conference reconstructions and one personal synthesis. These are not official slides or product benchmarks.

insights.title: Make knowledge reusable
insights.observation: Data access needs business definitions, relationships and expert interpretation.
insights.application: Capture approved knowledge once. Carry its sources and conditions into each relevant task.

insights.title: Choose a capable path
insights.observation: A task can use rules, retrieval, a small model or deeper reasoning.
insights.application: Compare complete task cost and quality. Route within permissions and freshness limits.

insights.title: Prove the operating model
insights.observation: Production work needs ownership, evaluation, lifecycle controls and recovery.
insights.application: Start with a bounded workflow. Establish a baseline and agreed expansion gates.

lenses.name: Cost
lenses.mechanism: Bound context size. Reuse valid views. Choose a capable route.
lenses.measure: All-in recurring cost per accepted task, plus one-time setup cost.
lenses.guardrail: Include review, rework, retrieval and operations. Token savings alone do not establish value.

lenses.name: Performance
lenses.mechanism: Use bounded decisions and fast paths. Escalate when the task needs more work.
lenses.measure: End-to-end median and p95 latency, throughput and retries at agreed load.
lenses.guardrail: p95 is the time within which 95% of measured tasks finish. Compare the same workload and quality gates.

lenses.name: Accuracy
lenses.goal: Preserve the meaning behind the answer
lenses.mechanism: Carry source links, dates, conditions and conflicts. Check derived statements.
lenses.measure: Domain-reviewed task acceptance, supported claims and appropriate abstention.
lenses.guardrail: Abstention means withholding a conclusion when evidence is insufficient. A correct format does not prove a correct answer.

lenses.name: Trust
lenses.mechanism: Enforce scope and permission. Show the evidence, owner and review decision.
lenses.measure: Boundary-test results, audit coverage, owner approval and user confidence.
lenses.guardrail: Measure user confidence separately from correctness. Model confidence cannot create authority.

scorecard.name: Cost
scorecard.metric: Recurring cost per accepted task; one-time setup; maintenance effort.
scorecard.trial: Run baseline and candidate on the same accepted-task target. Include digital costs and human handling.
scorecard.decision: Expand only when the agreed economic case holds after full cost readback.

scorecard.name: Performance
scorecard.metric: Median and p95 completion time; throughput; retries; recovery time.
scorecard.trial: Use the same workload, load and quality standard. Include retrieval, tools and review queues.
scorecard.decision: Meet the owner’s service target without hiding tail latency or failed tasks.

scorecard.name: Accuracy
scorecard.metric: Task acceptance; source correctness; stale/conflict detection; abstention.
scorecard.trial: Keep held-out cases separate from development cases. Use domain review and deterministic checks.
scorecard.decision: Meet agreed quality gates. Investigate failures before expanding scope.

scorecard.name: Trust
scorecard.metric: Scope isolation; permission enforcement; evidence coverage; reviewer decisions.
scorecard.trial: Test hostile source instructions, revoked access, cross-vault retrieval and audit readback.
scorecard.decision: Hold release for a material boundary failure. Assess user confidence separately.

businessCase.definition: Compare the same monthly number of accepted tasks. Accepted means the result passes the buyer’s task and quality criteria.
businessCase.formula: Attempts = accepted-task target ÷ acceptance rate. Monthly recurring cost = attempts × (digital cost + handling minutes × hourly rate ÷ 60) + fixed cost. Year-one net difference = 12 × monthly difference − one-time setup.
businessCase.limitation: Invented example assumptions, not measured product savings or a price quote. Rates and workload stay constant for the year-one estimate. Validate them in a pilot. Positive economics do not override quality or permission gates.
businessCase.costScope: Digital cost includes inference, retrieval, tools and variable infrastructure. Handling includes review, rework and escalation. Fixed cost includes licensing and operations. Setup is shown separately.
